newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope calls for lasting peace for Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Pope calls for lasting peace for Bosnia.

text.p: Pope John Paul, calling Sarajevo a "city of cemeteries", said on Wednesday that only dialogue and reconciliation among Bosnia's ethnic and religious communities could cement lasting peace.

In his first comments on Bosnia since his historic trip to Sarajevo last weekend, the 76-year-old leader of the world's Roman Catholic Church, said he had urged Moslems, Catholic Croats and Orthodox Christian Serbs to give and seek forgiveness.
"Let us forgive and let us ask forgiveness," the Pope said at his weekly general audience. "The path of reconciliation and dialogue is the only one which leads to lasting peace."

The 25-hour visit to Sarajevo was marred by the discovery just a few hours before the Pope's arrival last Saturday of anti-tank mines planted under a bridge along his route from the airport into the city. The devices, linked to a detonator, were defused.

The Pope said Bosnia's 1992-1995 war had turned Sarajevo into a "city of cemeteries", remarking on the thousands of graves he saw near the soccer stadium where he celebrated an open-air mass last Sunday.

The mass took place in a bitingly cold wind and snow but the Pontiff, who has suffered a string of health problems in recent years, showed no ill effects at Wednesday's audience, held in sunshine in St Peter's Square.
During meetings with representatives of Sarajevo's main religions, the Pope said he had witnessed a desire for peace.
"Peace, which comes from forgiveness and reconciliation is essential to every faith," he said.
"This spirit of unity, forgiveness and reconciliation ...was present at my meetings with representatives of the Orthodox, Islamic and Jewish communities," he said.
